narrative:
The model estimates a 39.0% probability that you will fail your final year. Although that is below a coin flip, it is high enough in this decision process to flag you as failing and require remedial courses rather than risk letting the year end without support.

The strongest factor driving that flag is your history of one past class failure, while students who passed typically had none. This pattern matters more than anything else in your profile, because it suggests the difficulty is not new. The next strongest factor is your absence record: you have zero absences, while students who passed averaged about 3.78. That works in your favor and pushes the prediction toward passing. The third factor is your father’s education; he completed secondary school, a level shared by about a quarter of students who passed, and this also modestly supports a passing outlook.

To improve, treat the remedial courses as a chance to break the prior-failure pattern. Keep your attendance strong, use your family’s support, and ask for targeted help in the subject you previously failed. Also consider reducing high weekend alcohol use and very high going-out time, and increase study time beyond two to five hours weekly.
